root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `xmlTextReaderFreeProp()` retires an xml:id attribute `cur`, the document ID table must no longer return that same attribute pointer for its ID value.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable no-DTD path skips `xmlTextReaderRemoveID(cur->parent->doc, cur)`, so immediately before the attribute is retired `xmlGetID(cur->parent->doc, cur->children->content)` still returns `cur`. The fixed code removes the xml:id entry first, so the same free-site executes with the ID table no longer pointing at the retiring attribute.

nodes.state: At the attribute-free site, the document ID table still returns `cur`, so retiring the attribute leaves a stale xml:id entry that names freed memory.
At `if (val->type == XML_NAMESPACE_DECL)`, `val` is the same freed `<m>` element recovered from the stale xml:id attribute, so the sink dereferences freed heap memory.

edges.relation: The same xml:id attribute pointer retired by `xmlTextReaderFreeProp()` is later reloaded from `doc->ids` by `xmlGetID(doc, ID)` and bound to `attr`.
The freed parent element stored in `cur->parent` before the attribute is retired is the same element later reloaded by `elem = attr->parent` after the stale xml:id attribute is returned.
The freed element recovered from the stale xml:id attribute is forwarded unchanged into `xmlXPathNodeSetAdd(ret, elem)` and becomes the sink operand `val`.
